incident-bot: ALERT: nebula-solutions (dedicated pool dp-72 eu-west-2) p99 latency > 2.8s for 7m. Threshold breached. Dash: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/REND/latency?var=pool=dp-72  Runbook: /runbooks/dedicated-pool-noisy-tenant
Sam (oncall): Acknowledged. Paging SREs. @Jin @Ravi please grab hot metrics (CPU, queue depth, kv cache hit) and open traces. Im starting the triage checklist.
Jin (SRE): Ack. Initial glance: p99 spike begins ~4375550800. p95 also up. One tenant (tenant T-9001) responsible for ~55% of recent token volume. Trace sample: https://traces.redwood.dev/trace/0xab3
Ravi (SRE Lead): Is it large single-stream context or many parallel short requests?
Jin (SRE): It's many concurrent long-context sessions with repeated regenerations. KV cache miss rate for T-9001 is 67% last 10m. dp-72 workers CPU avg 89% and queue depth spiking to 140.
Sam (oncall): Potential mitigations: 1) immediate tenant-rate-limit, 2) route tenant to a lower-memory variant, 3) enable aggressive prefix caching for tenant, 4) spin up hot standby nodes. Which do we do now?
Adele (oncall-2): Do rate-limit + model fallback now. Standby spin-up in parallel. I'll craft throttle rule.
AutoScale-Bot: Executing: `rictl pools scale --pool dp-72 --add 3` (async). Estimated warm time ~80s.
Jin (SRE): Applying temporary rate-limit for T-9001: `rictl routing set --tenant T-9001 --rate 400rpm --policy emergency --expires 20m`  Done.
Sam (oncall): Also applying model-fallback: route requests with >3000 tokens to nebula-medium-ctx instead of nebula-large-ctx. Command executed.
Maya (CS): Notifying Nebula account — preparing message: "We've detected high-volume regenerations from some sessions causing elevated latency; we've applied temporary throttles and fallback routing. Engineering is mitigating; will share updates." Sending now.
Ravi (SRE Lead): Monitor queue depth and KV eviction logs. Jin, tail worker logs for any OOMs or repeated cache evictions.
Jin (SRE): Tail excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T15:00:22Z dp-72 worker-4: req tenant=T-9001 ctx_size=5200 tokens=5100 latency=2970ms
2026-03-15T15:01:10Z dp-72 worker-2: cache_miss tenant=T-9001 key=ctx-113
2026-03-15T15:01:45Z dp-72 worker-7: throttle applied tenant=T-9001 rate=400rpm
```
Sam (oncall): AutoScale-Bot shows +3 nodes added, 2 are ready, third finishing startup. Adele, any warm-spare failover thresholds we should adjust?
Adele (oncall-2): Lowering failover queue threshold from 100 -> 50 to trigger faster spillover to warm nodes. Executing: `rictl pools set --pool dp-72 --failover-queue-threshold 50`
AutoScale-Bot: Updated failover threshold and marked new worker instances as joining pool.
Jin (SRE): After throttle+fallback+scale p99 dropped from 3.1s -> 950ms within 5m. Token rate from T-9001 decreased ~75%.
Maya (CS): Nebula replied: "Thanks for the quick mitigation. Can you confirm if any requests were dropped or retried on their side?" They asked about billing impact.
Ravi (SRE Lead): Note billing check in timeline — if SLO breach > 30m, escalate for credit review. For now, keep mitigation live until stable 15m.
Sam (oncall): I'll create a short incident timeline doc and capture the throttle/config commands for the postmortem. Jin, grab sample prompts + model outputs for eval.
Jin (SRE): Collecting 50 representative requests from T-9001 for quality regression testing.
Adele (oncall-2): Taking over handoff in 8m. Summary to pass: noisy tenant T-9001 causing KV cache pressure and CPU saturation -> mitigations applied: 400rpm temporary throttle, model fallback to nebula-medium-ctx for >3000 tokens, scaled pool +3, lowered failover threshold to 50. Customer notified. Monitoring.
incident-bot: STATE CHANGE: Mitigation detected at 4375551478 (p99 < SLO for 3m). Automated postmortem created: https://incidents.redwood.dev/4375551111  Please attach logs and timeline.
Maya (CS): Copy. I'll coordinate customer readout and attach customer impact note to the incident. Leaving monitoring to Adele. Update thread when stable for 20m then marking resolved."
